newsitem.title: USA: Dole formally concedes defeat in U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: Dole formally concedes defeat in U.S. election.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole on Tuesday formally conceded defeat to President Bill Clinton in the U.S. election and said he had telephoned Clinton to congratulate him.

Dole told cheering supporters at a hotel in Washington: "It hurts to lose an election, but stay involved and keep fighting the good fight." Echoing a statement he made throughout his campaign, he added: "I'm still the most optimistic man in America."

Dole, with his wife Elizabeth and daughter Robin at his side and struggling to keep his emotions in check after an arduous campaign that left him well beaten by Clinton, said: "I have never been prouder in my life than to have been the Republican nominee for the president of the United States."

He said: "I talked to President Clinton and I congratulated him." Gracious in defeat, he stilled those in his audience who booed at the name of Clinton, saying: "I've said repeatedly in this campaign the president was my opponent, not my enemy and I wish him well..."

He drew a laugh when he said: "I was just thinking on the way down the stairs that tomorrow will be the first day in my life when I don't have anything to do." Dole had been 35 years in Congress when he resigned as Senate Majority Leader in May to concentrate on his run for president.

He offered a line of consolation to his campaign aides and supporters when he declared that although the Republicans had lost the presidential race, "We're gonna keep the Senate, We're gonna keep the House (of Representatives)." Television networks predicted his party would retain control of both houses of Congress.
